subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should `openclaw doctor --lint` warn by default—and therefore report a non-clean lint result—when an operator has configured a positive byte guard that current runtime intentionally leaves inactive without transcript rotation?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically narrow and matches current runtime and docs, but whether this existing misconfiguration should affect the default lint contract is an operator-facing policy choice.

options.title: Accept the default warning
options.body: Merge the check so Doctor surfaces the documented no-op configuration before long-running sessions rely on it.

options.title: Keep the diagnostic opt-in
options.body: Require an explicit Doctor scope or deep check if maintainers do not want this configuration warning to change default lint output.

recommendation.title: Accept the default warning
recommendation.body: Merge the check so Doctor surfaces the documented no-op configuration before long-running sessions rely on it.
